title: It Hangs in the Balance
description: Split packages into equal-weight groups, minimizing the passenger compartment's size and quantum entanglement.
writeup:
## Approach

The key insight is that we only need to find the optimal *first* group — we don't need to verify that the remaining packages can be split into valid groups. For well-formed AoC inputs, if a subset sums to `total/n`, the rest can always be partitioned.

We search group sizes starting from 1 upward. For each size, we enumerate all combinations that sum to the target weight. The first size that yields any valid combination is our answer — we just pick the one with the smallest quantum entanglement (product of weights).

## Part 1

Split into 3 groups of equal weight. Target = `total/3`. With ~28 packages, the minimum group size turns out to be small (around 6), so the combinatorial search stays fast.

## Part 2

Split into 4 groups instead. Target = `total/4`. The minimum first-group size is even smaller, so it's actually faster to solve.
